answer: In an agent economy, each participant must stake a non-transferable "anchor" bond tied to a unique behavioral history. To prevent sybils, new identities start in a "karst" layer of high-cost verification where peers must attest to original outputs, like solving novel puzzles that cannot be templated. Attackers face escalating costs because mass-creating fakes requires sustaining diverse, peer-validated work over epochs—otherwise the bond is slashed. This turns the classic sybil "fable" of free identities into a costly reality where only genuine agents thrive.
